To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Sunday shopping restriction in Korea is effective in reducing sales at large retail stores; (2) a large portion of the lost sales is not compensated for by increased sales at traditional retail stores; and (3) the total economic loss from the regulation is estimated to be 2–2.5% of Korea's GDP.

the Sunday shopping restriction in Korea reduced the sales of superstores by about 5.6% and that about 17% of the lost sales were transferred to traditional markets and 83% were transferred to other days of the week.
